title: Reading lab: 1 Peter 1:3–5
subtitle: Read a blessing through participles and prepositional phrases.
overview: 1 Peter begins with a blessing whose central declaration is extended by participles, prepositional phrases, and purpose language. Build the sentence around its main praise.
Trace the relationship between mercy, new birth, hope, inheritance, and guarding without reducing every genitive to the same English “of.”

items.grc: εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
items.en: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

items.grc: ὁ κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος ἀναγεννήσας ἡμᾶς εἰς ἐλπίδα ζῶσαν δι᾽ ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
items.en: Who, according to his great mercy, gave us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
